subject: Urgent: Evidence request after latency/error threshold breach — Fintrix
messages:
From: Priya Desai <priya.desai@fintrix.com>
To: camila_reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tim Hargreaves <tim@fintrix.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production impact: sudden p99 latency and 5xx spike — need logs/chain-of-custody

Camila,

We hit a severe user-impacting incident during our morning region traffic run (US), roughly 09:45–10:15 PDT. Our telemetry shows p99 latency for generation requests jumped from ~850ms to >3.5s and a corresponding rise in 5xx responses that led to several downstream errors in our product. This affected our checkout flows for ~7% of users.

We need the following immediately for our postmortem and any regulatory review:
- Copy of all runtime logs for Fintrix tenant for 2027-05-28 08:00–11:00 PDT (request/response headers, status codes, and token counts)
- Any aggregated SLO/metrics snapshots (p50/p95/p99, error counts) for the same window
- List of Redwood employees or services that accessed or exported logs in that window (chain of custody)
- Retention timeline for raw request logs and any backups; were any log redaction or retention rules applied to our tenant?

We understand there may be a short delay, but please indicate ETA for delivery and whether you can share an executive-facing brief for our leadership.

Thanks,
Priya Desai
Director of Ops, Fintrix
priya.desai@fintrix.com

Thanks for the fast turn. We downloaded the ZIP and the CSVs — the p99 spike lines up with our traces (thanks for the correlation). A couple follow-ups from our compliance team:

- For executive review, can you produce a short (1-page) evidentiary summary that lists what was exported, who accessed it with timestamps, and copies of the relevant audit log lines? We need that by Monday morning EOD our time.

I'll also note our legal team may request a secure chain-of-custody attestation for any exports used in regulatory filings.

Regards,
Priya
